result.title: FlipVLA: Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action(VLA) Models Only Through Bit Flips
result.comment: 14 pages, including references and supplementary material
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions in real-world environments, making malicious model tampering a potential threat to physical safety. We study whether object-triggered backdoors can be implanted through a small, fixed set of parameter bit flips without retraining. The central challenge is to make persistent weight modifications disrupt trigger-present behavior while preserving performance on non-trigger inputs. We propose FlipVLA, a two-stage selector-amplifier method that exploits existing visual features within an FC-GELU-FC structure. The selector constructs a trigger-dependent response in a selected channel, using GELU to attenuate background activity. The amplifier modifies a connected downstream weight to convert this response into an action-relevant perturbation. Channel screening and discrete bit search construct both components under a limited modification budget. Experiments on OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7 across four LIBERO suites achieve attack success rates of 90.22% to 100%, with task success decreasing by at most 1.5 percentage points on clean scenes.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究无需重训练、仅靠少量参数比特翻转即可在 VLA 模型中植入由物体触发后门的方法 FlipVLA，通过「选择器—放大器」两阶段定位并放大 FC-GELU-FC 结构中已有的视觉特征通道，在保持干净场景性能的同时实现高攻击成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对单一通道视觉响应做筛选并放大为下游动作扰动的做法，可能作为核查「内部视觉细节是否被答案实际使用」及视觉证据因果贡献的探针线索，但属安全攻击视角，与 LVR 推理机制的直接联系需阅读后判断。
